name: Scott Syndrome

criteria.description: Demonstration of defective platelet procoagulant activity on flow cytometry or functional assays
Reduced or absent phosphatidylserine exposure on activated platelets
Personal or family history of mucocutaneous bleeding or hemorrhagic diathesis
Normal platelet count and normal platelet aggregation studies excluding other platelet function disorders
Identification of mutations in ANO6 (TMEM16F) gene if available

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of defective platelet procoagulant activity and reduced phosphatidylserine exposure combined with bleeding history
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of other platelet function disorders and coagulation factor deficiencies.

pathognomonic.notes: Detected by specialized platelet function assays

pathognomonic.symptomName: Reduced phosphatidylserine exposure on activated platelets

common.notes: Includes easy bruising, epistaxis, and gum bleeding

common.symptomName: Prolonged bleeding after trauma or surgery

laboratory: Defective platelet procoagulant activity on flow cytometry
Absent or reduced phosphatidylserine exposure on activated platelets
imaging: Imaging may be required to assess bleeding complications such as intracranial hemorrhage
genetic: Mutations in ANO6 (TMEM16F) gene associated with defective phospholipid scrambling
other: Family history of bleeding disorder may be present

distinguishingFeatures: Defect in platelet aggregation due to integrin αIIbβ3 deficiency
Defect in platelet adhesion due to GPIb deficiency

redFlags: Severe mucocutaneous bleeding disproportionate to platelet count
Prolonged bleeding after minor trauma or surgery
Intracranial hemorrhage or other life-threatening bleeding
references: Scott syndrome: a rare bleeding disorder caused by defective platelet procoagulant activity. Blood Reviews. 2019.
Anoctamin 6 (TMEM16F) mutations in Scott syndrome. Blood. 2010.
Platelet procoagulant activity and bleeding disorders: clinical and laboratory aspects. Haematologica. 2017.
